However, little is known about the pathogenic mechanisms underlying the action of homocysteine. The present study investigated the in vitro ability of homocysteine to affect trophoblast gonadotropin secretion and to induce cell death. In primary human trophoblast cells, homocysteine treatment (20 μmol/L) resulted in cellular flattening and enlargement, extension of pseudopodia, and cellular vacuolization.
